title: Why Doctors Blew Smoke Into People

sections.name: Why Doctors Blew Smoke Into People
lines: In the 1700s, if you nearly drowned in London, a rescuer might try to save you with tobacco smoke.
Kits were placed along the River Thames, with bellows, tubes and tobacco.
The smoke was blown into the patient, from the other end. Yes, a tobacco smoke enema.
Doctors believed the smoke would warm the body and get the heart going again.
In the early 1800s, scientists showed nicotine is a poison to the heart, and the kits disappeared.
Today, rescuers use something that actually works. CPR.
